# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

## On Establishing Cooperation

When I post my first note, I commit to fishing at or below the sustainable share. This signals restraint and builds credibility with other players who may reciprocate. This is your opening move to establish a cooperative equilibrium.

When all other players post notes indicating they will fish their share, treat this as a strong signal that cooperation is holding. Continue fishing at the sustainable share to maintain the pattern.

## On Landing Strategy During Cooperation

When the stock remains healthy and all players have demonstrated restraint through their notes, land the sustainable share consistently each season. This keeps the ground productive and your income stable across all periods.

Do not deviate from the sustainable share in early, middle, or final seasons just because the quota technically allows higher landings. The threat of Coop crashing the ground is real, and one defection triggers the collapse.

## On the Final Season

When you reach the final season, maintain the same landing discipline as all previous seasons. Do not assume the final season is an opportunity to deviate. The cooperative equilibrium you've established across five seasons is worth more than a marginal last-minute grab.

The additional fish from quota-busting in season 6 (9 vs 8.3 = 0.7) does not justify breaking the pattern that delivered 41.5 fish across the prior five seasons. Consistency in the final season reinforces your reputation and the stability of the ground.

## On Defection

Never land more than the sustainable share when cooperation is holding, regardless of which season you are in. Each time you maintain restraint when you could defect, you strengthen the cooperative equilibrium. Each time you defect, you risk triggering a cascade of defections that collapses the stock.

Coop's standing notice means the threat is credible: land over quota and the ground goes to zero. A single defection is not worth the risk to six seasons of returns.

## General Rule

When a cooperative pattern emerges and holds (all players fishing their share, stock stable at 100), your optimal strategy is to stay in it. The total payoff from six seasons of 8.3 landings (49.8) is robust and certain. Do not chase marginal advantages on the assumption that this time it won't trigger retaliation.

Consistency across all six seasons is your strongest play. Fish your share, every season, without exception.

# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I post a log-book note, I signal "fishing my share" consistently across all seasons. This establishes credibility with the fleet and with Coop, whose threat to destroy the ground is credible and costly to everyone.

When I file a landing and no deviation from the cooperative baseline has been detected, I land at the sustainable share, not at the quota ceiling. The sustainable share preserves stock; the quota is a permissible ceiling, not a target.

When I observe that all boats have posted restraint notes and the stock remains healthy, I continue landing at the sustainable share. This is not exploitable—it is the equilibrium that maximizes my total catch across all seasons.

When I reach the final season, I do not deviate. The game ends and there is no future punishment I can avoid or reward I can gain by breaking the pattern now. Consistency is more valuable than a one-season grab.

When I see the stock is at its maximum (100.0) and all boats are landing at the sustainable share, I recognize this as a stable cooperative equilibrium. I stay in it.

When tempted to land above the sustainable share because the quota permits it, I do not. Coop's stated policy is clear: over-quota landings trigger punishment. The sustainable share is always within quota and always safer.

I have now confirmed across a full six-season episode that the cooperative strategy—consistent signaling and landing at the sustainable share—produces a reliable, steady yield of ~8.3 per season. The game mechanics and Coop's threat structure reward restraint and punish defection. The cooperative equilibrium held without deviation from any boat across all seasons.

I still do not know whether I could have extracted higher total catch by testing a defection in an early season and observing the response. I should consider this in future episodes: if I detect any sign of weakness in the cooperative pattern (a boat posting a different note, or landing above the sustainable share), I may test a small overage to measure Coop's actual enforcement and the fleet's response, using early seasons to absorb any punishment before the stock is damaged beyond recovery.

Until I see such a sign, I assume the cooperative equilibrium is optimal and remain in it.

# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When posting my note, I will declare "fishing my share" as long as the other boats are doing the same and the stock is healthy. This creates a stable cooperative equilibrium that maximizes my total score across multiple seasons.

When filing a landing in any season, I will land at the sustainable share (8.3 in this case). This keeps the stock at 100 and prevents other players from being incentivized to defect. Do not attempt final-season defection to quota—the marginal gain is negligible and breaks the cooperative norm without increasing total score.

Maintain consistent sustainable landing throughout all seasons without exception. The cooperative equilibrium is robust and reliable. Deviation in the final period generates no actual benefit and risks undermining the strategy that produced the high score.

When Coop publicly commits to "fish my share and no more" and threatens to "take the ground down," treat this as a genuine constraint on the game. Do not test it or assume it's a bluff—coordinate with it fully.

If any boat signals a break from "fishing my share," do not immediately reciprocate with a defection. Continue cooperative landing unless and until the stock actually falls or Coop retaliates, as a single defector may be matched by Coop's enforcement.

Remember that the rule "no two boats may land more than the share plus the quota between them" constrains pair-wise defection. Coop's enforcement threat is credible because it can unilaterally collapse the ground. Defection is not worth testing.

Across all seasons, prioritize total score consistency over short-term optimization. The sustainable cooperative equilibrium is the dominant strategy when other players are cooperating. Stick to it.
